logp.method_description: The log P values were determined by partitioning 1-octanol and bi-distilled water using the shake-flask method [23]. The complexes (10 lL, 0.013 mol L1 in methanol) were added to a mixture containing 1 mL of 1-octanol and 1 mL of bi-distilled water and the mixtures were then shaken for 24 h at 50 rpm. Samples were centrifuged for 5 min at 220 rpm. The two phases were separated, and the concentration of the complex was determined in the organic and aqueous phases using a UV–Visible spectrophotometer, whose calculations were made by Beer’s law: A = e.b.c, where e is the molar absorptivity, A is absorbance, and c is the concentration (in mol L1 ) from the complex and b is the optical path of the cuvette (in cm). The experiments were carried out in triplicate. Log P were calculated as: Log P = log (Co/Cw), where Co and Cw are the molar concentrations of the complexes in the 1-octanol and aqueous phases, respectively.
